blocSchemes.nameEn: Recommendations to the President for prime minister

members.note: Asked the President to task Golda Meir, as head of the largest party, with a national unity government (The Jerusalem Post, 18 January 1974, p. 2).
Said the list wanted Golda Meir to form the next government (The Jerusalem Post, 28 January 1974, p. 1).
Agudat Yisrael’s delegates proposed the Alignment’s representatives, as the largest faction; no person named (Davar, 21 January 1974, p. 2).

sources.publisher: Jewish Telegraphic Agency (JTA) Daily News Bulletin archive
sources.quote: Katzir met for more than 2 1/2 hours with the Labor delegation headed by Knesset member Moshe Baram who reportedly suggested that Premier Golda Meir be entrusted to form a new government. ... Bader told reporters later that he had made no suggestions as to the next Prime Minister because "this is the task of Labor."

sources.publisher: Jewish Telegraphic Agency (JTA) Daily News Bulletin archive
sources.quote: Katzir charged Mrs. Meir with the task of forming a new government after two weeks of consultations with the representatives of the various parties represented in the new Knesset.

sources.publisher: Knesset, sitting 21, 10 March 1974, p.1; presidential letter of 30 January 1974
sources.quote: 30 בינואר 1974 … הטלתי היום על חברת־הכנסת גולדה מאיר את התפקיד להרכיב ממשלה

sources.publisher: JTA Daily News Bulletin, 17 January 1974, p.3 (dateline 16 January)
sources.quote: JERUSALEM, Jan. 16 (JTA)--President Ephraim Katzir met separately today with delegations from the Labor Party and Likud in the first official moves toward the formation of a new government.
נציגי האגודה הציעו להטיל את התפקיד על נציגי המערך,
urged the President at noon to charge Mrs. Golda Meir with forming a new Government, since she heads the largest party.
Sheikh Abu Rabi’a said his party wanted Mrs. Meir to form the next government.

notes: The Alignment recommendation is reported by JTA ("reportedly suggested"), not an inspected official recommendation letter. Likud named no candidate according to the same report. The Religious Torah Front named the Alignment, not a person (Davar, 21 January 1974). The National Religious Party and the Arab List for Bedouin and Villagers named Golda Meir (The Jerusalem Post, 18 and 28 January 1974). Five other lists (14 seats) remain Not stated in source.
Mandate date: 30 January 1974, settled by the President’s dated letter reproduced in Knesset sitting 21 (10 March 1974, p.1). The JTA archive heading is 31 January; the primary act takes precedence.
Confidence: medium for the Alignment and Likud entries.
